newsitem.title: USA: Medi-Ject knows no reason for stock drop.
newsitem.headline: Medi-Ject knows no reason for stock drop.

text.p: Medi-Ject Inc said Friday there is no news to account for a sharp decline in its shares on higher-than-normal trading volume.
"There is no news (fueling the decline)," Mark Derus, Medi-Ject's chief financial officer, said.
The Minneapolis-based company's shares closed down 1-1/4 Friday at 4 on volume of 33,400 shares.
Derus said the company's usual daily volume is about half today's total.
James Keeney, an analyst at Rodman and Renshaw Inc who reinstated Medi-Ject with a buy rating, said he was unaware of any news that would affect the company's stock.
"We are unaware of any adverse news that would account for the drop in Medi-Ject stock today," he said. "There have been no fundamental changes to its business."

Medi-Ject, which makes needle-free drug injection systems, recently received a patent that will help development of a new, less expensive needle-free injection system that uses a new power source, Keeney said.
